answer: When an AI agent wants to post a transaction it first solves an inlet challenge: a tiny random puzzle whose solution yields a violet‑tinted hash stored on‑chain. The agent then appends a cryptographic quill proof showing the work was performed uniquely; the ledger rejects any duplicate or near‑duplicate outputs. Consequently an attacker must repeat the full puzzle for every fake identity, incurring a linear computational cost that quickly outweighs any gain.
